data.gender_notes: Khan is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A title given to a king, chief, or ruler. The name Khan carries the meaning “Ruler, Chief, Lord” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Persian, Urdu, Turkish. Parents who choose Khan usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler, chief, lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Khan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ruler, Chief, Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Khan total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_english.long_meaning: The term Khan is used in Islamic history and culture to refer to tribal leaders and rulers, symbolizing power and authority. In Islamic tradition, the title Khan is given to those who possess great power and authority, such as Nuh. In some Islamic traditions, Khan is also referred to as Khan Khanan. Khan is also associated with the military and political aspects of Islam, and is considered a symbol of Islam's power and authority. In Islamic tradition, Khan is also considered a title of honor and respect, and is often used to refer to those who possess great wisdom and knowledge. The name Khan has been used in various cultures and traditions throughout history, and continues to be an important title in Islamic culture today.
